analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: Bank Earnings This Morning, The outlook for corporate equity supply and demand in 2027, CPI Preview, S&P Implied Correlation at the Lows, EU Sovereign Sensitive Financials
key_insights: JPM Q3 results were viewed as largely in line. Deposit costs rose faster than the Street expected (+7 bps QoQ vs +1 bp) and FICC trading missed by 10%.

JPM cut buybacks to about $1bn from $6.7bn in Q2. The note reads this as a shift to deploy capital into risk-weighted assets organically rather than repurchase stock at a steep premium to tangible book value.
JPM's 2027 NII ex-markets guidance of $107bn (+10% YoY) is the main bull anchor and drove constructive pre-market trading.
WFC's headline EPS beat was discounted as low quality because it was tax-driven. A PPNR miss of about 3% leaves bulls without a positive catalyst.
WFC CET1 fell 30 bps to 10.0% under AOCI pressure and buybacks slowed to $2.5bn. Analysts expect the Street to model further repurchase reductions.

Rising rates and AOCI marks put bank capital back in focus. Lower-capital peers (WFC at 10.0% vs JPM at 13.9%) and super-regionals are likely forced to pause or curtail buybacks, while money-center banks keep flexibility to fund AI infrastructure buildouts.

Equity issuance in 2026 is on track for the largest total since 2021, at roughly $430bn year to date (+98% YoY). GS reads this as a return to normal after four years of muted activity rather than an issuance boom.
GS expects $600bn of primary corporate equity issuance in 2027 (0.8% of equity market cap) and does not expect the added supply to derail the bull market.

GS equity analysts forecast hyperscaler capex of about $1.2tn next year against $1.1tn of operating cash flow. Credit strategists estimate 35% of capex will be debt-funded, which implies over $400bn of issuance.
GS expects US corporate buybacks of $1.7tn in 2027, up from $1.5tn this year. If rates keep rising, a narrower gap between the cost of debt and the cost of equity will likely restrain buyback growth.

GS forecasts September core CPI at +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%) and +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%). Headline is forecast at +0.59% m/m (consensus +0.6%) and +3.70% y/y (consensus +3.6%, August +3.40%), with energy up 5.0% on higher retail gasoline.
GS flags that a 10bp downside surprise on core CPI would be meaningful for rates. The forecast is consistent with a 0.20% m/m increase in September core PCE.
3m S&P implied correlation sits below the 2nd percentile of the last twenty years. Options are pricing wide dispersion through year-end, and GS PB data shows very low net exposures.

If investors re-risk, winners and losers will be separated by their ability to beat already elevated expectations. Low implied correlation is global, with 3m levels in the bottom decile across most equity markets.

European sovereign stress hit an inflection point last week. French OAT-Bund spreads are the widest since 2012, Italian spreads widened after Rome revised its deficit forecasts (+1.2% of GDP cumulative through 2027-2028), Spain called snap elections for 29 November, and UK gilt yields touched multi-year highs ahead of the Fall Budget.
The ECB has TPI and balance sheet runoff flexibility, but GS says these are not a substitute for credible fiscal trajectories. GS expects sovereign volatility to stay elevated over the coming months.

GSXESOVR is a liquid basket of domestically exposed banks from France, Italy, Greece, Belgium and the UK, plus an insurance sleeve of about 15%. Insurers hold large sovereign portfolios under Solvency II, which adds a transmission channel through mark-to-market and capital requirements.

GSXESOVR is down 12% from its peak and has underperformed SX7P by 350bps since mid-August. SX7P gives diluted sovereign exposure because its top weights (HSBC, Santander, BBVA) earn mostly outside Europe.

earnings_insights: JPM Q3 (reported 10/13): deposit costs +7 bps QoQ vs +1 bp Street expectation, FICC trading about 10% below expectations, buybacks cut to about $1bn from $6.7bn in Q2, 2027 NII ex-markets guidance $107bn (+10% YoY).
WFC Q3 (reported 10/13): headline EPS beat attributed to tax effects and viewed as low quality, PPNR about 3% below expectations, CET1 down 30 bps to 10.0%, buybacks $2.5bn.
GS flags 3Q earnings season as the setup for dispersion, with winners and losers separated by their ability to exceed already elevated expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: 2027 NII ex-markets guidance of $107bn (+10% YoY) anchors the bull thesis, and the buyback cut redeploys capital into organic RWA growth rather than repurchases at a steep premium to tangible book.
tension_points.bear_case: Deposit costs rose +7 bps QoQ vs +1 bp expected and FICC trading missed by 10%.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects $600bn of 2027 primary equity issuance, only 0.8% of market cap, and does not expect it to derail the bull market. Buybacks of $1.7tn offset supply.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising rates usually pose a challenge for equity prices and issuance, and a narrowing gap between the cost of debt and equity may restrain buyback growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Interest rates continuing to rise, which would narrow the gap between the cost of debt and cost of equity and slow buyback growth.
